content: The Feedback and Audit Tools consist of a set of interconnected quality improvement tools designed to periodically evaluate adherence to the World Health Organization (WHO) Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) and Selected Practice Recommendations (SPR) guidelines. These tools include the following components: 1. Provider Survey: This tool assesses knowledge or practice gaps among clinical providers. It can be conducted anonymously to evaluate overall practices or linked to individual providers to identify specific coaching or training needs. The survey may be repeated periodically to monitor progress. 2. Contraceptive Method Mix Assessment: This tool allows local implementation teams or clinic managers to monitor the distribution of contraceptive methods being provided to clients. It can help identify gaps in method availability or usage. 3. Measuring Adherence to Guidance Tool: The implementation of these tools is not static. As the WHO MEC/SPR guidelines are introduced, updated, or adapted to specific settings, it is essential to monitor the process and provide feedback to providers, clinics, and programs. The data collected through these assessments can inform targeted interventions, such as individual coaching, training, technical assistance, or programmatic and policy changes. The Provider Survey includes demographic questions and evaluates provider practices. For example: Questions 1–4 collect demographic information. Questions 5–6 assess whether providers have been trained on specific methods. If many providers lack training, formal training programs may be necessary. Question 7 explores the availability of contraceptive methods in the clinic. If methods are unavailable or limited, clinic management should investigate the reasons behind this. The Interpretation Guide accompanying the Provider Survey identifies key concepts being evaluated and links them to the WHO MEC/SPR guidelines. The Contraceptive Method Mix Assessment Tool helps monitor the range of contraceptive methods used in clinics. By reviewing method usage logs, clinics can identify potential gaps and address them through targeted interventions, such as client surveys, focus groups, or outreach programs. These discussions should be conducted in a non-punitive, quality improvement-focused environment. The Implementation Guide Toolkit provides strategies for addressing gaps in care identified through the surveys and assessments. Examples include: Group meetings to discuss results and explore solutions. Observations of clinic practices and provider-client interactions by clinic managers or implementation teams. Use of mystery clients (external observers acting as clients) to report on their experiences. The Measuring Adherence to Guidance Tool is used to monitor the successful implementation of WHO family planning guidelines at national, facility, and provider levels. Key steps include: 1. Setting targets based on metrics relevant to the organizational level and setting. 2. Developing strategies, tools, and processes to collect data on these metrics. 3. Collecting and recording data at each level. 4. Using the data to identify gaps and implement targeted interventions.
